## Problem

pm-ops#271 fixes #268, #269 and #270 in the canonical release path: `scripts/release-continuation.ts` and the reusable `daily-release.yml`. No external package calls the reusable workflow, though. Each of these 37 packages carries its own copy of `release.yml`, so they keep the old behaviour until their copies are updated:

pm-ado, pm-beads, pm-brand, pm-brief, pm-case, pm-changelog, pm-cli, pm-context, pm-csv, pm-evidence, pm-gantt-chart, pm-github, pm-glossary, pm-graph, pm-http, pm-hypothesis, pm-jev, pm-jira, pm-linear, pm-lint, pm-memory, pm-presets, pm-reduce, pm-review, pm-rl, pm-rlm, pm-rust, pm-screen, pm-slack, pm-slack-standup, pm-starter, pm-swarm, pm-todos, pm-ts-starter, pm-unit, pm-vcs, pm-web

`docs/release-diagnosis-propagation.md` (in #271) has the inventory.

## Expected

- The fixes reach every copy through the **existing template path**, never through hand copies, as #268 asks. Either the canonical template update flows to the packages through their normal update mechanism, or the packages switch to calling the reusable workflow at a pinned SHA, so future fixes need only a pin bump.
- Each package's next Daily Release shows the fresh blocker diagnosis, the bounded receipt parsing and the publishing-job signer.

## Acceptance

- None of the 37 copies still contains the sticky `awaiting_approval` diagnosis, the end-anchored receipt parse, or the preparation-pin signer derivation.
- The scheduled-workflow watch reports no Daily Release failures of these three classes.

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-14T12:56:54Z)

> Nov 14 fleet receipts for the existing sticky-approval diagnosis: [Slack #198 release job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-slack/actions/runs/43586534742/job/132422140928) and [Todos #200 release job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-todos/actions/runs/43585920892/job/132420245758) each logged three successful run approvals. Their final merge attempts report the required Node checks queued and `failing: none`, but the timeout asks for workflow approval again. Neither job reached publication or tagging. These are additional rollout fixtures for the same stale classification, not proof the product tests failed. Verify each copied caller reports queued checks rather than asking the owner to approve a second time.

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-14T21:16:36Z)
>
> **Cross-repository OIDC proven (2026-11-14 20:4xZ).** The first pilot, pm-jira#209, merged, so pm-jira's `release.yml` is now a thin caller of `unbraind/pm-ops/.github/workflows/daily-release.yml@7687a35 # v2026.11.14`. Its first dispatched run, [43639146392](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jira/actions/runs/43639146392), passed reconcile, prepare and request, and its OIDC preflight logged `npm accepted this workflow's identity for pm-jira.`. The npm trusted publisher on the caller's own `release.yml` is enough; no npm-side change was needed.
> 
> The rollout to the remaining packages can proceed. pm-lint#85 stays a draft until pm-changelog#337/#354 is released. Packages without an npm trusted publisher yet (pm-vcs, pm-rl, pm-review, pm-rlm) will still fail at the OIDC step until the owner configures one.

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-14T22:39:04Z)

> Additional rollout acceptance evidence: separate npm identity, packaged version coherence, and actual publication. The [Jira pilot run](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jira/actions/runs/43639146392) passed prepare/request, including the OIDC identity check, but skipped release and Bun verification.
> 
> I independently ran the [pinned workflow's exact prepare step](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/blob/7687a35d7522482bd8361d60dbc2589e9afbc81c/.github/workflows/daily-release.yml) at synthetic `2026.11.99` with published `pm-ops@2026.11.14`, built each scratch source copy, packed without lifecycle reruns, then imported the entry named in the extracted manifest. Results (package / manifest / exported runtime):
> 
> - [Jira merged #209](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jira/pull/209), `dfc4349d`: .99 / .99 / .99, both with its preserved prepare hook and with the hook omitted in a control. The shared helper already handles Jira's directly quoted `defineExtension` shape; the pilot does not exercise plain-object callers.
> - [Context #232](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/pull/232#issuecomment-6885025816), `a93fcc1e`: .99 / .99 / .13.
> - [CSV #257](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-csv/pull/257#issuecomment-6885029777), `003e7a12`: .99 / .99 / .13.
> 
> No registry or provider mutation. These are local build/pack/import results, not full release gates. For the existing rollout, add this scratch next-version equality check for extension callers that remove custom stamping (including the distinct [Graph #214 case](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-graph/pull/214#issuecomment-6884584260)); keep package-specific ownership on those PRs. A successful identity check or build by itself won't catch a stale exported version.

> Graph rollout follow-through: [#214 merged](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-graph/pull/214) at `27fb62af2820270410c90d3d2fee290ca54a3027`. Its tree is identical to the reviewed PR head (`041cc5fb47736430eeb493034d818ae63a582476`), including the exact [previously tested entrypoint](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-graph/pull/214#issuecomment-6884584260) and the [thin caller with no prepare-script](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-graph/blob/27fb62af2820270410c90d3d2fee290ca54a3027/.github/workflows/release.yml). Current main is coherently .12, and official npm latest is .12; exact .14 returns 404. The separately prepared open [.14 candidate #213](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-graph/pull/213) at `19d533b3` has matching .14 source/package/manifest. The risk is a **new** candidate prepared through the merged caller, not an observed bad publication or proof that #213 is broken.
> 
> The next configured preparation slot is 03:23 UTC; :41 is reconciliation-only, and a pending transaction can suppress new preparation. Please preserve Graph's runtime stamping or gate the next eligible fresh candidate on packed package/manifest/runtime equality. Check continuation disposition for #213 rather than assuming the schedule will create or publish a new candidate.

> **@unbraind** (2026-11-15T02:33:19Z)
>
> Jira pilot update: the shared workflow has now completed an actual cross-repository trusted publication, not just the OIDC preflight. The [scheduled continuation's release job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jira/actions/runs/43662547054/job/132656469714) consumed the verified candidate, passed the publish-time OIDC check, published with [signed provenance](https://search.sigstore.dev/?logIndex=3891807638), pushed the tag, created the [GitHub Release](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jira/releases/tag/v2026.11.14), and marked the durable intent complete. Post-publication Bun verification was still queued when checked.
> 
> Independent artifact check: [the official npm registry version](https://registry.npmjs.org/pm-jira/2026.11.14) exposes SLSA provenance, its tarball matches registry SHA-512, and the packed package, manifest, and compiled extension version literal all say `2026.11.14`. This proves Jira's prepared candidate and signer path only. It does not clear the previously documented stamping checks for newly prepared Graph/Context/CSV artifacts or prove other publishers are configured.
